title: Structured light for addressable two-qubit gates in medium-sized ion crystals: modeling motional and dephasing errors
authors: Pablo Viñas, Alan Kahan, Tommaso Faorlin, Lorenz Panzl, Phoebe Grosser, Thomas Monz, Alejandro Bermudez
abstract: Geometric phase gates with addressed laser radiation are widely used in trapped-ion quantum computers to drive high-fidelity entangling gates on an arbitrary qubit pair of a larger ion chain. Such programmable connectivity exploits the collective phonons to mediate the desired interaction, while simultaneously achieving robustness to their thermal fluctuations by a careful calibration of the gate time with respect to the laser and vibrational-mode frequencies. Crosstalk errors can arise when the spectator qubits, which should ideally remain idle during the gate, are partially driven by the laser fields. The minimal crosstalk, which is set by the laser beam size on the spectator ions, can be achieved when the addressing beams propagate perpendicular to the ion chain. However, this results in exciting the radial phonons, and can complicate achieving high-fidelities as the ion chain grows due to the so-called spectral mode crowding. In this work, we present the theoretical description of a scheme recently implemented by Faorlin et $al.$. This scheme overcomes these complications by engineering addressable state-dependent forces along the ion-chain with laser beams that propagate perpendicular to it through the use of structured light gradients. In this way, one can excite the axial phonons and avoid the spectral mode crowding, while simultaneously minimizing the crosstalk. We present a detailed derivation of the entangling gate scheme, together with analytical closed-form expressions for the leading contribution to the gate error caused by thermal motional fluctuations and dephasing noise. Our results confirm that such fluctuations account for up to 93$\%$ of the error budget under the operating conditions of the gate implemented by Faorlin et $al.$. We identify target parameters to reduce the motional error from the reported $10^{-3}$ to the $10^{-5}$ level.
summary: This paper theoretically details a method using structured light gradients to implement high-fidelity, addressable two-qubit gates in medium-sized ion crystals. By engineering forces that excite axial phonons, the scheme avoids spectral mode crowding issues associated with standard perpendicular addressing. The analysis provides quantitative error budgets, showing that thermal and dephasing noise are the dominant error sources, and suggests parameters to push fidelity to the $10^{-5}$ level.
main_problem: The primary challenge is maintaining high-fidelity entangling gates in large trapped-ion quantum processors while mitigating crosstalk and spectral mode crowding.
main_result: The use of structured light gradients allows for the excitation of axial phonons while minimizing crosstalk, theoretically enabling gate fidelities that scale robustly to larger ion chains.
method: The authors provide a detailed theoretical derivation, deriving closed-form expressions for error contributions from thermal motional fluctuations and dephasing noise.
model_or_system: The system is a trapped-ion crystal where qubits interact via geometric phase gates mediated by collective vibrational modes. The dynamics are modeled using Hamiltonians involving structured light coupling and free vibrational modes.
key_observables: Gate fidelity, error budget contributions from thermal motional fluctuations and dephasing noise, and the ability to maintain high fidelity up to N=20 ions.
important_parameters: Detuning ($\delta$), effective Lamb-Dicke parameter ($\eta$), and the target reduction of motional error from $10^{-3}$ to $10^{-5}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations such as the Taylor expansion of the Rabi frequency and the assumption of negligible spontaneous decay.
figures_summary: Figure 6 compares experimental state infidelity to theoretical predictions for Barium and Calcium ions, showing the impact of time-correlated dephasing.
paper_structure: The paper reviews geometric phase gates, details the structured-light scheme for engineering addressable state-dependent forces, and concludes with a thorough analytical error analysis covering thermal, dephasing, and magnetic noise.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the scaling limitations of trapped-ion quantum computing by proposing a novel optical addressing scheme that mitigates mode crowding, a critical issue in large quantum processors.
